questions.question: Can internal audit help find problems or risks early? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Can internal audit help find problems or risks early? [An] / [CO1]
  • Yes, internal audit can help identify problems and risks at an early stage. By regularly
  • reviewing processes, controls, and operations, internal auditors detect weaknesses before
  • they become major issues. This helps management take preventive actions and improve
  • overall efficiency and security.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: How does the IIA support the global internal auding profession? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• How does the IIA support the global internal auding profession? [U] / [CO1]
  • The IIA (Institute of Internal Auditors) supports the global internal auditing profession
  • by setting professional standards, offering certifications like CIA, and providing training
  • and research resources. It also promotes best practices, ethical guidelines, and a global
  • network for knowledge sharing and professional growth.

questions.question: Why should internal auditors study the existing control systems? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Why should internal auditors study the existing control systems? [An] / [CO2]
  • Internal auditors should study existing control systems to understand how well they
  • protect assets, ensure accuracy, and support operational efficiency. By examining
  • current controls, auditors can identify weaknesses, risks, or gaps. This helps recommend
  • improvements to strengthen the organization’s overall internal control environment.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is the relationship between internal audit and accountability mechanisms in corporations? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the relationship between internal audit and accountability mechanisms in
  • corporations? [U] / [CO1]
  • The relationship between internal audit and accountability mechanisms in corporations
  • is interconnected: (1) internal audit provides independent evaluation of internal controls,
  • ensuring operations follow policies and regulations; (2) it strengthens accountability by
  • detecting errors, fraud, and inefficiencies and requiring management to address them; (3)
  • it supports transparent and reliable financial reporting, which is essential for holding
  • leaders responsible; (4) it enhances risk management by identifying weaknesses that
  • could undermine accountability; and (5) it informs the board and audit committee,
  • enabling effective oversight and reinforcing a culture of responsibility and ethical
  • conduct within the corporation.
  • . 10. Discuss how the Internal Audit Charter supports effective internal auditing process
  • [U] / [CO1]
  • The Internal Audit Charter supports an effective internal auditing process by (1)clearly
  • defining the purpose, authority, and responsibility of the internal audit function; (2)
  • establishing the audit team's independence from management, which is essential for
  • objective evaluations; (3) outlining the scope of audit activities to ensure
  • comprehensive coverage of risk, controls, and governance; (4) granting auditors
  • unrestricted access to records, personnel, and physical properties necessary for thorough
  • examinations; (5) setting reporting lines to senior management and the audit committee
  • to strengthen oversight; (6) providing a framework for accountability and performance
  • standards; and (7) ensuring alignment of internal audit activities with organizational
  • goals and regulatory requirements, thereby enhancing the overall effectiveness and
  • credibility of the audit process.

questions.question: What are the main responsibilities of the Chief Audit Executive (CAE) under the charter? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What are the main responsibilities of the Chief Audit Executive (CAE) under the
  • charter? [An] / [CO4]
  • The Chief Audit Executive’s (CAE) main responsibilities under the charter include: (1)
  • developing a risk-based internal audit plan and ensuring its execution; (2) ensuring the
  • internal audit activity maintains independence, objectivity, and alignment with
  • professional standards; (3) managing audit resources and assigning work to competent
  • staff; (4) communicating audit results, significant risks, and control issues to senior
  • management and the board; (5) coordinating with external auditors and other assurance
  • providers to optimize coverage; (6) reporting on the performance, effectiveness, and
  • resource needs of the internal audit function; and (7) ensuring follow-up on management
  • action plans to address audit observations.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe the challenges faced by internal auditors while auditing government organizations. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the challenges faced by internal auditors while audit in government
  • organizations. [U] / [CO1]
  • Internal auditors in government organizations face several challenges, including:
  • (1) bureaucratic delays and rigid administrative procedures that slow audit activities;
  • (2) limited access to complete and timely data due to poor documentation or restrictive
  • information practices; (3) political influence or pressure that may compromise auditor
  • independence; (4) resource constraints such as inadequate staffing, skills gaps, or
  • outdated technology; (5) resistance from departments or officials who may perceive
  • audits as fault-finding; (6) complex regulatory frameworks and frequent policy
  • changes that increase compliance difficulty; and (7) challenges in implementing
  • recommendations due to slow decision-making and weak accountability mechanisms.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What factors should be considered before accepting an internal audit engagement? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What factors should be considered before accepting an internal audit engagement?
  • [An] / [CO2]
  • Before accepting an internal audit engagement, the following factors should be
  • considered: (1) the independence and objectivity of the internal audit team to ensure no
  • conflicts of interest; (2) the competence, skills, and resources required to perform the
  • audit effectively; (3) clarity of the audit scope, objectives, expectations, and timelines;
  • (4) understanding of the organization’s business, risks, internal controls, and regulatory
  • environment; (5) management’s support and the availability of necessary information
  • and access; (6) potential limitations or restrictions that may affect audit quality; and (7)
  • legal, ethical, and professional requirements relevant to the engagement.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What is meant by an existing control system? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What is meant by an existing control system? [U] / [CO2]
  • An existing control system refers to the set of processes and mechanisms already in
  • place within an organization to ensure effective operations, reliable reporting, and
  • compliance with laws and policies, and includes: (1) established policies, procedures,
  • and standard operating processes; (2) manual and automated controls designed to
  • prevent or detect errors, fraud, and inefficiencies; (3) roles, responsibilities, and
  • authorization structures that promote accountability; (4) risk management practices
  • that identify, assess, and mitigate risks; (5) monitoring activities such as supervision
  • and internal checks; and (6) information and communication systems that support
  • timely and accurate decision-making.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: What are the sources of information used to identify risks during audit planning? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What are the sources of information used to identify risks during audit planning?
  • [U] /
  • [CO3]
  • Sources of information used to identify risks during audit planning include:
  • (1) previous audit reports and follow-up results that highlight recurring issues;
  • (2) discussions and interviews with management and key process owners;
  • (3) organizational policies, procedures, and strategic plans;
  • (4) financial statements, performance data, and operational records;
  • (5) industry trends, regulatory updates, and external reports;
  • (6) internal control assessments and risk registers maintained by the organization; and
  • (7) observations from walkthroughs, site visits, and preliminary analytical reviews.

questions.question: Explain the evolution and development of internal auditing as a profession. / [CO1] [6x5 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the evolution and development to internal auditing as a profession.
  • [U] / [CO1]
  • The evolution and development of internal auditing as a profession can be explained as
  • follows: (1) it began in the early 20th century as a clerical activity focused mainly on
  • checking financial transactions; (2) gradually, organizations recognized the need for
  • internal checks to prevent fraud and errors, expanding the auditor’s role; (3) the
  • formation of the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) in 1941 formalized internal
  • auditing as a recognized profession; (4) over time, internal audit shifted from
  • compliance and financial verification to assessing internal controls and operational
  • efficiency; (5) the introduction of the International Standards for the Professional
  • Practice of Internal Auditing strengthened professionalism and global consistency; (6)
  • in recent decades, the role evolved further toward risk-based auditing and governance
  • assurance; and (7) today, internal auditing is seen as a strategic function that provides
  • insight, advice, and value addition to organizational decision-making.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
